data.name: NoUsableForecast
data.value: No usable forecast, so there is no plan for today. The mode works like Solar instead: it charges from live surplus only once the home battery is full.

data.name: NoChargeableWindow
data.value: Today has no charging window: the sun never stays above the charger's minimum for long enough, or the home battery needs all of it. The car waits.

data.name: TodayGives
data.value: Today gives the car about {0}, in a window from {1:HH:mm} to {2:HH:mm}.

data.name: TargetMet
data.value: Target met: {0} of the {1} asked for has reached the car. The charger has been released.

data.name: Headline
data.comment: {0} is the energy still to deliver, {1} the departure time.

data.name: AlreadyInCar
data.value: {0} of the {1} asked for is already in the car.
data.comment: Appended to Headline, after a space.

data.name: MoreThanCanDeliver
data.value: {0} by {1} is more than the {2} left can deliver. Charging at full power from now, the car will get about {3} — {4} short.

data.name: LeavingInstead
data.value: Leaving at {0} instead would allow the full amount.
data.comment: Appended to MoreThanCanDeliver, after a space.

data.name: BatteryHeldOut
data.value: The home battery is kept out while the grid charges the car, so it is not drained into a charge that will fall short anyway.

data.name: ForecastCoversAll
data.value: The forecast covers all of it: {0} from surplus {1}. No grid import is planned.

data.name: BatteryKeepsPriority
data.value: The home battery keeps priority throughout: whenever the car draws more than the panels produce, the discharge hold turns on, so the battery never feeds the car.

data.name: NoUsableForecastTargeted
data.value: There is no usable forecast for this window, so the plan assumes the grid supplies all of it. Any surplus that does appear is used first, and the plan is recalculated on the next poll.

data.name: SunAndGrid
data.value: The sun should cover {0} of it {1}, and the grid the remaining {2}. Instead of charging at full power and finishing early, the car charges at about {3} across the window, so the charger draws close to what the panels produce and only the difference is bought.

data.name: UnusableSurplus
data.value: {0} of surplus is forecast for this window, but it never exceeds the charger's 6 A minimum, so the car cannot charge on it alone. It is still useful: while the sun is up the charger stays at that minimum, the panels supply what they can, and only the difference is bought — about {1} from the grid on average.

data.name: AllFromGrid
data.value: No surplus is forecast before then, so the {0} still needed all comes from the grid, at about {1} across the window. With no sun to wait for, there is nothing to gain by delaying, and spreading the charge leaves time to recover if something drops out.

data.name: HoldingNow
data.value: Everything up to the rest level is in the car, and the last {0} is held back until {1}. Nothing is wrong — the charger is idle on purpose, so the car reaches its target shortly before you leave instead of sitting full all night. Sun arriving before then is not used; that is the cost of this choice.

data.name: HoldingLater
data.value: The last {0} is held back until {1}, so the car finishes just before you leave rather than hours early. Until then, everything up to the rest level charges normally, from the sun whenever there is sun.

data.name: ChargeModeTip
data.value: Starting any mode below switches the charger to Fast; Off stops the car, whatever mode was running. Nothing survives a restart — the service starts in Off and writes nothing until you press something here. Fast (no battery) and Targeted switch off by themselves when the car is done, and Solar + grid when the day's useful sun is over; the line above updates by itself.

data.name: HoldTip
data.value: Applies to every mode, which is why it sits above them: it stops the home battery supplying the house, so the car charges from PV and the grid while the battery can still charge from surplus. It shows the last command written successfully, not a reading from the device — if a write fails, it switches back off by itself.

data.name: StartedAt
data.value: started from the Web UI at {0}

data.name: StoppedAt
data.value: stopped from the Web UI at {0}

data.name: SolarIntro
data.value: Charges from surplus the house isn’t using, once the home battery is full.

data.name: SolarTip
data.value: Charges from whatever the panels produce that the house is not using. The home battery comes first: this mode waits until it is full, or has stopped taking charge, then follows the surplus up and down, and pauses when there is not enough to hold the charger's minimum current.

data.name: StartSolarTip
data.value: Switches the charger to Fast and lets the surplus drive it. Nothing else to set — the current is whatever the sun leaves over, recalculated every poll.

data.name: SolarSurplusHint
data.value: PV left after household consumption — the 3-minute average this mode acts on. Blank while a mode that does not use surplus is running.

data.name: BatterySocGateHint
data.value: The gate for this mode: the car gets nothing until the home battery is full.

data.name: EvPowerHint
data.value: What the charger reports the car actually drawing right now — not a setpoint.

data.name: TargetCurrentHint
data.value: The current this mode chose this cycle, before writing it. Blank when not charging.

data.name: SolarGridIntro
data.value: Follows the sun; when the surplus is small, the grid tops it up to the charger’s minimum.

data.name: SolarGridTip
data.value: Charges from the sun, with help from the grid. While the surplus stays above your minimum, the car follows it. When the surplus alone is too small for the charger's minimum current, the grid tops it up to that minimum, and the home battery is not used. The home battery does not need to be full. When the surplus drops below your minimum, the car pauses — averaged over a few minutes, so a passing cloud does not stop it — and once the forecast shows no more sun today above the minimum, the mode switches itself off.

data.name: StartSolarGridTip
data.value: Switches the charger to Fast and lets the surplus drive it. Ends by itself when the day's useful sun is over, when the car stops drawing, or when it is unplugged.

data.name: MinSurplusTip
data.value: Below this, the car pauses instead of using the grid. The grid adds at most the charger's minimum power (about 4.1 kW at 6 A on three phases) minus this value; set it at or above that and the grid never helps. The rest of today's forecast must also exceed this value for the mode to keep running. Not kept after a restart.

data.name: SolarGridLowTariffHint
data.value: In high tariff the car waits, sun or not, and charges as above once low tariff starts. The mode still ends when the day's useful sun is over, so a low tariff that starts after dark charges nothing here. Not kept after a restart.

data.name: SunUntilHint
data.value: When the forecast says the surplus stops exceeding your minimum today — the time this mode switches itself off, if the live surplus agrees. Shown only while this mode is running.

data.name: GridPowerTopUpHint
data.value: Positive while importing. While the grid tops up a small surplus, this is roughly the top-up.

data.name: UntilFullTip
data.value: Keeps one session going over several days, for a car left at home over a weekend or a week: one sunny afternoon rarely fills it, three usually do. Daytime charging is unchanged. When the mode would end for the day, it pauses the charger overnight instead and starts again with the next day's sun. It ends when the car is full, when it is unplugged, or when you press Off. A session with this on is resumed after a restart.

data.name: UntilFullDay
data.value: Running until full: day {0} of this session.

data.name: NoTariffYet
data.value: Set up a tariff in {0} first; until then there is nothing to wait for.

data.name: LowTariffIgnoredNote
data.value: On, but ignored: no tariff is configured, so it charges at any hour.

data.name: ForecastedIntro
data.value: Charges from surplus, guided by the forecast so the home battery still fills by evening.

data.name: ForecastedTip
data.value: Charges from surplus like {0}, but replaces the fixed battery-full rule with the Solcast forecast: the plan decides how much of today's remaining sun the car may take, so the home battery still reaches 100% by the evening deadline. The midday peak goes to the car; the morning and evening sun stays with the house and the battery.

data.name: StartForecastedTip
data.value: When no usable forecast is available, it does not refuse to charge: it works like Solar and charges from live surplus only once the home battery is full.

data.name: WhereChargeStopsTip
data.value: This mode does not take an amount: it charges the car from the surplus the forecast says the home battery will not need, until the car's own charge limit stops it. To keep the car below full, set that limit in the car. To {0} for an amount by a set time, use {1}: when the forecast covers it in time, it charges from the sun only, and buys from the grid only if the sun falls short.

data.name: MinBatterySocTip
data.value: The lowest the home battery may go while it helps charge the car. When it gets there, the car pauses until the battery has recovered by the resume margin below. The plan may keep a higher floor when the forecast says the battery needs it to be full by the deadline. Shared with the Targeted mode, so a change here applies there too. Not kept after a restart.

data.name: ResumeMarginTip
data.value: How far above the floor the battery must recover before a paused session restarts. Raise it if the car starts and stops repeatedly on a borderline day. Not kept after a restart.

data.name: PlanOnlyWhileForecasted
data.value: The day plan is shown only while {0} is the active charge mode. Current mode: {1}.

data.name: PlanStateHint
data.value: Why the plan decided what it did — the same line as in the log.

data.name: ChargeWindowHint
data.value: The next part of today forecast to stay above the charger's minimum power long enough to be worth starting. 'none' when today has no such window.

data.name: EvBudgetHint
data.value: How much of today's remaining sun the car may take, counting only periods when the surplus is above the charger's minimum power.

data.name: ProjectedShortfallHint
data.value: How far today's forecast falls short of covering the house and filling the home battery. Above zero, reaching 100% by evening is at risk. The car is not included — it only gets what is left over.

data.name: SurplusSpillHint
data.value: Remaining surplus the home battery has no room for — what is still to come minus what it can absorb. At 100% that is all of it, and every watt is exported unless the car takes it. That is why the battery may lend to the car against a much smaller surplus.

data.name: LoanHeadroomHint
data.value: How much the battery may lend right now: the room between its SOC and the floor, capped by the spill. Zero when SOC is at the floor, or when the battery can still absorb all the remaining sun.

data.name: RequiredFloorHint
data.value: The SOC the battery must not drop below right now, so the remaining sun can still bring it back to 100% by the deadline. When battery SOC falls to this line, the car pauses.

data.name: ForecastRemainingHint
data.value: PV still forecast for today, at the configured confidence band and already adjusted for forecast accuracy.

data.name: TomorrowForecastHint
data.value: Tomorrow's forecast production. For information only: it helps judge whether today's shortfall is worth waiting out.

data.name: ForecastAccuracyHint
data.value: Actual production compared with the forecast so far today. 100% means exactly on target. The rest of today's forecast is scaled by this, and a large miss that persists makes the plan untrusted.

data.name: LoanedTodayHint
data.value: Energy the home battery has lent the car today, so a surplus below the charger's minimum could still reach it. Resets at local midnight.

data.name: IntoCarSincePlugged
data.value: {0} into the car since it was plugged in.

data.name: FastIntro
data.value: As fast as the installation allows, with the home battery kept out — expect grid import.

data.name: FastTip
data.value: Charges as fast as the installation allows and keeps the home battery out of it. The current is fixed at the configured maximum whatever the sun is doing: PV covers what it can and the grid covers the rest, so expect to import. The discharge hold turns on when the charge starts and off when it ends — you can switch it off in between if you want the battery to help.

data.name: EnergyNeededTip
data.value: Measured at the charger, from the moment you press the button.

data.name: ReadyByTip
data.value: With no time set, the charge starts straight away. With a time, the charge is delayed and starts as late as possible while still finishing before you leave — so a car charged above 80% spends minutes there instead of the whole night, which is what actually wears the battery. It still charges at full power; only the start moves. To remove a time, open the calendar and press Clear.

data.name: FastLowTariffHint
data.value: In high tariff the car waits, and it charges at full power once low tariff starts. The charger starts a car by itself when it is plugged in, so a car plugged in during high tariff draws power briefly until the next poll stops it. Not kept after a restart.

data.name: FastEvPowerHint
data.value: What the car is actually drawing right now, as reported by the charger — not a setpoint. This drops when the car decides it is full.

data.name: FastEvCurrentHint
data.value: Charging current calculated from the charger's measured power: what the car really takes. It can be below the maximum if the car limits it.

data.name: ActiveCurrentHint
data.value: The charger's setpoint read back from the hardware: what it is actually set to.

data.name: FastGridPowerHint
data.value: Positive while importing from the grid, negative while exporting. In this mode it is the price of the speed.

data.name: DeliveredHint
data.value: Energy delivered so far against the amount requested, metered at the charger since this charge started. The mode stops itself when it gets there.

data.name: BasisEnergyHint
data.value: The charge stops when that much has been delivered, or earlier if the car stops first.

data.name: BasisSocHint
data.value: Converted to kilowatt-hours once, when you press the button. A later reading from the car does not change a charge already in progress.

data.name: BasisFullHint
data.value: The car decides: the charge runs until it reaches its own charge limit and stops drawing.

data.name: BasisFullNoSocHint
data.value: The car decides: the charge runs until it reaches its own charge limit and stops drawing. A battery target needs the car's capacity in Vehicle:BatteryCapacityKWh and a reading from the car.

data.name: EndsFullHint
data.value: Ends by itself: when the car stops drawing because it has reached its own charge limit, the current drops to the pause level and the mode returns to Off, which releases the hold.

data.name: EndsAmountHint
data.value: Ends by itself: at the amount above, or earlier if the car stops drawing. Either way the current drops to the pause level and the mode returns to Off, which releases the hold.

data.name: NoUsableSoc
data.value: No usable SOC reading to calculate the difference from.

data.name: AlreadyAt
data.value: The car is already at {0} — nothing to do.

data.name: SocConversion
data.value: From {0} now, that is about {1} at the charger: {2} usable capacity, with {3} of the energy metered at the charger reaching the cells.

data.name: FastDelivered
data.value: The {0} requested has been delivered; the charge is stopping.

data.name: FastProgress
data.value: {0} of {1} is in the car; {2} to go before it stops by itself.

data.name: PowerMaximum
data.value: {0} (the installation's maximum — the car has not drawn yet)

data.name: NotEnoughTime
data.value: Not enough time: about {0} of this will not fit before {1:HH:mm}. Charging at full power from now, at {2}.

data.name: WaitingUntil
data.value: Waiting until {0:HH:mm}, then charging at full power: {1} at {2} takes about {3}, and the car is needed by {4:HH:mm}.

data.name: ChargingToBeReady
data.value: Charging at full power to be ready by {0:HH:mm}: {1} to go at {2}.

data.name: TargetedPlanStateHint
data.value: Complete: the target is met. Solar: the forecast covers it with no import. Solar + grid: the sun covers what it can and the grid supplies the rest at a steady pace. Maximum: there is not enough time, so everything available is used.

data.name: StillNeededHint
data.value: The requested amount minus what the charger has measured as delivered since it started.

data.name: DeliveredSoFarHint
data.value: Measured at the charger, so if the car takes less than requested, the next poll simply schedules more grid charging.

data.name: ForecastSurplusHint
data.value: All the surplus forecast for this window, after the house and the home battery's share — whether or not the car can charge on it alone.

data.name: FromSunHint
data.value: The part of the surplus above that the car can actually charge on alone. Zero does not mean no sun: it means no half hour exceeds the charger's 6 A minimum. That sun is still used while the charger runs at its minimum, and only the difference is bought from the grid.

data.name: FromGridHint
data.value: What the sun cannot cover. Recalculated every poll, so a better day than forecast reduces this before the rest is bought.

data.name: ChargePaceHint
data.value: The average power the grid must supply to meet the target: what is still needed, minus the sun forecast to reach the car, spread over the time left. The charger runs at this plus whatever the panels produce, so extra sun is free and lowers the pace later. Zero means the forecast covers the whole target.

data.name: ChargingFromHint
data.value: When grid-supplied charging starts. The charge is spread across the window instead of running at full power, because the charger can only use the sun that shines while it is running.

data.name: ExpectedByDepartureHint
data.value: What will actually reach the car. Less than requested only when there is not enough time left.

data.name: ShortfallHint
data.value: How far the plan falls short of the request. Anything above zero means the departure is too soon for the amount requested.

data.name: HeldBackHint
data.value: The last part of the target, scheduled to finish just before departure instead of whenever the sun allows — so the car does not sit at a high state of charge all night. Everything below it charges normally.

data.name: ReleasedAtHint
data.value: When the held-back part starts. Calculated from the charger's maximum power plus a safety margin; if the car charges more slowly, the pace rises on the next poll, and Shortfall shows it if even that is not enough.

data.name: BatterySocFloorHint
data.value: Below this, the sun goes to the home battery and the car gets only what it needs for the deadline, from the grid. Never lower than your Minimum battery SOC; higher when the forecast leaves the battery too little sun to refill.

data.name: ReadyByHint
data.value: The time the plan aims for: your departure minus a safety margin.

data.name: ReportedByCar
data.comment: {0} is how old the reading is ("12 min").

data.name: ReportedByCarVia
data.value: Reported by the car {0} ago via {1}.
data.comment: {1} is the name of the feed the reading came from.

data.name: JustInTimeExtra
data.comment: The pacing option with what it costs: {0} is the extra grid energy, signed ("+2.1 kWh").

data.name: TargetedIntro
data.value: Say how much and by when; forecast sun goes first, the grid covers the rest as late as possible.

data.name: TargetedTip
data.value: Say how much the car needs and by when, then check the plan before starting. The plan uses every kilowatt-hour of forecast surplus the home battery has not already claimed, and buys the rest from the grid as late as possible while still finishing in time.

data.name: StaleCheck
data.value: Stale — older than {0}, so the feed may have stopped. Check these figures against the car before planning with them.

data.name: CarBatteryHint
data.value: The car's own state of charge, as its cloud service last reported it. Not the home battery.

data.name: RangeHint
data.value: The car's own estimate of its remaining range, based on its recent consumption. Display only — no plan uses it — but it tells you whether the target you are about to set is enough for the trip.

data.name: PluggedInHint
data.value: What the charger sees at its connector, and what the car reports about its socket. The charger is faster and is what the controller acts on; the car can be hours behind.

data.name: CarChargeStateHint
data.value: What the car reports it is doing: Idle, Charging, Complete, or Unknown when it does not report.

data.name: AimingAtTip
data.value: Either way, the target is measured in kilowatt-hours at the charger. A battery target is converted once, when you start — a later reading from the car does not change a target already in progress.

data.name: EnergyNeededStartTip
data.value: Measured at the charger, from the moment you press Start.

data.name: PacingTip
data.value: Both finish by the departure. {0} spreads the charge across the window and also takes every watt of sun above that pace, so the target is usually met well before you leave. {1} charges up to the rest level the same way, then holds the last part back so the car does not sit full overnight — this costs grid energy, because sun is not used while it waits.

data.name: SunOnlyTip
data.value: Nothing is bought from the grid. Whatever the sun cannot deliver by the departure is shown as a shortfall, not imported — the preview shows how much before you start. A cloud the 3-minute average has not caught up with can still draw a little from the grid while the car runs at its minimum, so expect close to zero, not exactly zero.

data.name: SunOnlyNoJustInTime
data.value: Just in time is off while this is ticked: holding the last part back with no grid to cover a cloudy hour can only lose sun.

data.name: TargetedLowTariffHint
data.value: In high tariff the car waits, sun or not, and the plan counts only on low-tariff hours before the departure. Whatever does not fit in them is shown as a shortfall — the preview shows how much before you start. The charger starts a car by itself when it is plugged in, so a car plugged in during high tariff draws power briefly until the next poll stops it.

data.name: SunOnlyNoLowTariff
data.value: Low tariff only is off while Sun only is ticked: sun only buys nothing from the grid at any hour.

data.name: ReadyByTargetTip
data.value: Charging finishes a few minutes before this time, so the car is ready and no longer drawing. At most {0} ahead.

data.name: MinBatterySocTargetedTip
data.value: Below this level the home battery comes first: the sun charges it, and the car gets only what it needs from the grid to be ready on time. At or above it, the car also takes the solar surplus. The home battery never charges the car in this mode. On a poor-sun day the plan may keep a higher floor so the battery can still refill. Shared with the Forecasted mode, so a change here applies there too. Not kept after a restart.

data.name: PreviewTip
data.value: The preview writes nothing — it asks the same planner the poll loop runs what would happen if you started now. The request does not survive a restart of the service: if it restarts overnight, the car stops charging and you will not be told.

data.name: IfYouStartNow
data.value: The plan, if you start now

data.name: NoPollForPlan
data.value: No poll has completed yet, so there is nothing to build a plan from — no battery SOC, no house load, no forecast tied to the current time. You can still start the target; the plan appears after the first poll.

data.name: PlanOnlyWhileTargeted
data.value: The plan is only shown while {0} is the active charge mode. Current mode: {1}.

data.name: AskingSoc
data.value: Charging to {0} from the {1} the car last reported: {2} at the charger, including charging losses.

data.name: NoSocForRest
data.value: No usable SOC reading to work out the rest level from.

data.name: AlreadyAboveRest
data.value: The car is already at {0}, at or above the {1} rest level, so the whole charge is held back and none of it starts before the release time.

data.name: FinishesBelowRest
data.value: This target finishes at about {0}, at or below the {1} rest level, so there is nothing to hold back and the charge runs as it would with Cheapest.

data.name: RestExplained
data.value: The car charges from the sun up to {0} whenever there is sun, then waits. The last {1} — about {2} to {3} — is scheduled to finish just before you leave.

data.name: HoldCostsNothing
data.value: Holding back the last part costs nothing here — the forecast has no sun it would miss.

data.name: HoldCost
data.value: Just in time buys about {0} more from the grid than the cheapest charge would, because sun is not used while the last part waits. In return, the car sits at {1} overnight instead of at its target.

data.name: ForecastReason
data.comment: {0} is why the forecast says what it says, in lower case.
